name: Vector
summary: A row vector of the integers or rationals in Q (over the rationals if any is not an integer).
differs: Vectors over rings other than the integers and the rationals are refused.
Dividing a vector over the integers, and assigning an entry (v[i] := x), are refused.

name: Vector
summary: A row vector over R (the integers or the rationals) of the elements of Q; v * A multiplies it by a matrix.

examples.code: v := Vector(Rationals(), [1, 1]); A := Matrix(Rationals(), 2, 2, [1, 2, 3, 4]); v * A; v * A^2;

differs: Vectors over rings other than the integers and the rationals are refused.
Dividing a vector over the integers, and assigning an entry (v[i] := x), are refused.

name: Solution
summary: The vector v with v * A = w (Magma's row convention), over A's ring; an error when there is none.

examples.code: A := Matrix(Rationals(), 2, 2, [1, 2, 3, 4]); Solution(A, Vector(Rationals(), [4, 6])); Solution(Transpose(A), Vector(Rationals(), [5, 11]));

differs: A system with more than one solution (a singular A) is refused: Magma returns a particular solution of its own choosing.
Magma's second return value, the kernel of A, is not returned.

name: VectorSpace
summary: The full vector space of degree n over the rationals: V.i its i-th unit vector, V![...] a vector, Dimension(V) and Basis(V).

examples.code: V := VectorSpace(Rationals(), 3); V![1, 2, 3] + V.2; Dimension(V); V.1 in V;

differs: Only over the rationals (RSpace: the integers too); other rings and fields are refused, as are subspaces and vectors of degree 0.
A set of two or more vectors is not printed or iterated over (Magma lists it in an order of its own).

name: KSpace
summary: The full vector space of degree n over the rationals, the same as VectorSpace(K, n).

examples.code: K := KSpace(Rationals(), 2); K; K eq VectorSpace(Rationals(), 2);
examples.expected:
Full Vector space of degree 2 over Rational Field
true

differs: Only over the rationals (RSpace: the integers too); other rings and fields are refused, as are subspaces and vectors of degree 0.

name: RSpace
summary: The full space of row vectors of degree n over the integers (over the rationals, the vector space).

examples.expected:
Full RSpace of degree 2 over Integer Ring
( 1 -3)
(4 5)

differs: Only over the rationals (RSpace: the integers too); other rings and fields are refused, as are subspaces and vectors of degree 0.

name: Generators
summary: The set of the unit vectors of a full vector space.
differs: Only of full vector spaces; of groups and other structures it is refused.
The set is not printed or iterated over when it has two or more vectors (Magma lists it in an order of its own).

name: Zero
summary: The zero of the integers, the rationals or a full vector space.
differs: Only of the integers, the rationals and full vector spaces (of degree at least 1); other structures are refused.

name: Matrix
summary: The m by n matrix over R whose entries, row by row, are the elements of Q (each coerced into R).
differs: Matrices over the integers, the rationals and finite fields only (an extension field of more than 2^20 elements is refused); a matrix with no rows or no columns is refused.

name: Matrix
summary: The matrix over R whose rows are the sequences in Q.
differs: Matrices over the integers, the rationals and finite fields only (an extension field of more than 2^20 elements is refused); a matrix with no rows or no columns is refused.

name: Determinant
summary: The determinant of a square matrix.
differs: Over a finite field, eliminations of more than 2*10^6 entry products (about 125 rows) are refused, as are products and powers past that work.

name: Rank
differs: Over a finite field, eliminations of more than 2*10^6 entry products (about 125 rows) are refused, as are products and powers past that work.

name: Transpose
summary: The transpose of a square matrix.

name: CharacteristicPolynomial
summary: The characteristic polynomial of a square matrix, in a new polynomial ring.
differs: Matrices over finite fields only: over the integers and the rationals it is refused.
Over a finite field, eliminations of more than 2*10^6 entry products (about 125 rows) are refused, as are products and powers past that work.

name: Submatrix
signature: (<Mtrx> A, <RngIntElt> i, <RngIntElt> j, <RngIntElt> p, <RngIntElt> q) -> Mtrx
summary: The p by q block of the matrix A whose top left entry is A[i][j].
differs: A block with no rows or no columns is refused.
